name: Gold sales and settlement
summary: Gold sales are the company's only revenue. When the refinery finishes refining a doré shipment it credits the fine gold and silver to the company's metal account and sends an outturn statement. The treasury and tax manager in Toronto checks the outturn against the mine's shipment advice, proposes how many ounces to sell, gets the chief financial officer's approval, asks bullion banks for bids and sells at spot; the metal moves to the bank and US dollars arrive two business days later. A corporate accountant matches the trade confirmation and the cash, records revenue and refining charges, and the sales record feeds royalties, financial reporting and the cash forecast. Delays come from outturn variances that need the mine's or an umpire's input, the CFO's availability and market hours, and the manual matching of trades, metal transfers and cash across portals.

baseline.org_archetype: A 300-person single-mine Ontario gold producer listed on the TSX that sells all refined gold at spot to Canadian bullion banks, with no gold or currency hedges in 2020-2021.
baseline.notes: Modelled on a single-mine northern Ontario gold producer (Eagle River mine and mill near Wawa) as described in the organisation file; site practice from the Eagle River technical reports where they say it.

unit_of_work: one gold sale (the refined ounces from one refinery outturn, sold in one or more spot trades)
trigger: The refinery issues an outturn statement crediting refined gold and silver from a doré shipment to the company's metal account.
end_state: The ounces are sold, the US dollar proceeds are received and matched, revenue and refining charges are booked, and the sales record and cash forecast are updated.

volume.seasonality: Follows shipments, two to four a month, with some outturns sold in more than one trade; slightly more trades near quarter end when cash is managed for reporting.

evidence.note: Gold sold: 88,423 oz in 2019, 91,229 oz in 2020, 118,501 oz in 2021 including Kiena (wdomda2021), about 7,600 oz a month for the single-mine period. The number of sales per month is the author's estimate.

Organisation file role (1 people). Runs every step from outturn check to trade and cash forecast. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (1 people). Approves the sale plan; in 2020-2021 the company had no hedges, so approvals cover timing and size of spot sales. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (2 people). Matches confirmations and cash and books the sale, keeping trading and recording apart. Not listed for this process in the organisation file. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

Organisation file role (1 people). Reviews the revenue journal. Not listed for this process in the organisation file. Loaded cost from the organisation file: base wage times 1.30 for staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.

steps.name: Refinery issues outturn statement
steps.description: The refinery finishes melting, sampling and assaying the shipment and emails its outturn statement with each bar's received weight, gold and silver assays, payable ounces, refining charges, and the date the fine ounces were credited to the company's metal account.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Final metal values are settled on the receiver's weights and assays (lbmavar2017).

steps.name: Confirm ounces credited to the metal account
steps.description: The treasury and tax manager logs into the refinery or bank metal-account portal and checks that the fine gold and silver ounces on the outturn have been credited and are free to sell.

error.defect_description: Ounces of a different shipment taken as this one.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Check outturn against the shipment advice
steps.description: The manager compares bar by bar the refinery's received weights, assays and payable ounces with the mine's shipment advice, checks the payable percentage and refining charge against the refining contract, and flags any shortfall beyond the agreed tolerance.

error.defect_description: Charge rate not checked against the contract.

control.basis: Refining agreement terms: payable gold percentage, charges and splitting limits checked on every outturn

evidence.note: Neighbouring mine's terms: 99.96% gold payable and 3.25 per oz refining and transport (island2020); results differing beyond agreed limits go to negotiation or umpire (lbmavar2017). Share with variance: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Query variance with the mill
steps.description: The manager emails the mill superintendent the bar-by-bar differences and asks for the gold room weights, bar sample assays and any re-assay, and asks the refinery for its sample results.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Mill explains or disputes the variance
steps.description: The mill superintendent checks the gold room scale record and the lab's bar assays, asks for a re-assay of retained bar samples if needed, and replies whether to accept the refinery figures or request an umpire assay.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for umpire assay
steps.description: A split of the refinery's sample goes to an independent umpire laboratory agreed in the contract; the ounces not in dispute can be sold meanwhile, and the final figure is set by the umpire result.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Settlement delayed until values are agreed by negotiation or umpire analysis (lbmavar2017). Duration: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Propose ounces and timing to sell
steps.description: The manager checks the spot price, the cash forecast and the metal held, and writes a short email to the CFO proposing how many ounces to sell now and whether to hold some for a better price or for quarter-end cash.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: No gold price hedges or forward exchange contracts in 2020-2021, so sales are spot decisions (wdofs2021). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: CFO approves the sale
steps.description: The CFO reads the proposal, may ask for part of the metal to be held, and approves the ounces and price limits by email.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Treasury policy and delegation of authority: CFO approval of metal sales before the trader executes

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Request bids from bullion banks
steps.description: During London or New York trading hours the manager phones or messages the dealing desks of two or three Canadian banks with the ounces and settlement location and asks for spot bids in US dollars per ounce.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Gold is sold exclusively to financial institutions (wdofs2021); spot gold is quoted in US dollars per troy ounce (lbmaotc). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Execute spot sale
steps.description: The manager accepts the best bid, confirms ounces, price and value date with the dealer and writes a trade ticket with the counterparty, ounces, price and settlement instructions.

error.defect_description: Ounces or value date written wrong on the ticket.

evidence.note: Spot trades deliver metal and currency two business days after the trade (lbmaotc). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Instruct metal transfer to the bank
steps.description: The manager instructs the refinery or the custodian holding the metal account to transfer the sold fine ounces to the buying bank's account for the value date, through the portal or a signed instruction.

error.defect_description: Transfer sent to the wrong account.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Match the bank's trade confirmation
steps.description: The corporate accountant, who did not trade, matches the bank's written confirmation to the trade ticket and the CFO's approval for counterparty, ounces, price, value date and settlement instructions, and raises any break with the manager.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: independent confirmation matching for treasury trades

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Wait for settlement
steps.description: On the value date the metal leaves the company's account and the bank pays the US dollar proceeds into the company's account.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Delivery of currency and metal is effected two business days after the transaction date (lbmaotc).

steps.name: Confirm cash received
steps.description: The corporate accountant checks the US dollar account in the bank portal, matches the receipt to the confirmation, and chases the bank or the refinery when cash or metal movement is short or late.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Chase late or short settlement
steps.description: The accountant and the manager email and phone the bank's settlements team and the refinery to trace the metal transfer and the payment, and book any late interest or charges.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Convert US dollars as needed
steps.description: The manager decides with the cash forecast how much of the US dollar proceeds to convert to Canadian dollars at spot with the bank for site payments, and books the conversion; with no forward contracts, the rest stays in US dollars.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Gold is priced in US dollars and the company had no forward exchange contracts in 2020-2021 (wdofs2021). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record the sale in the ledger
steps.description: The corporate accountant books revenue at the transaction price when control passes to the bank, the refining charges, the silver by-product revenue and the relief of gold inventory, and the foreign exchange on the conversion.

error.defect_description: Sale booked in the wrong period near month end.

evidence.note: Revenue recognised when control of the metal transfers to the customer; silver is a by-product; gold inventory carried at cost (wdofs2021). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review and approve the revenue journal
steps.description: The corporate controller reviews the journal against the confirmation, the outturn and the bank statement and approves it, checking the period cut-off.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (NI 52-109): independent review of revenue journals and period cut-off

evidence.note: Revenue recognition indicators include right to payment, legal title and transfer of physical possession (wdofs2021). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Update the sales record and royalty base
steps.description: The accountant adds the sale to the sales register with ounces, price, proceeds in both currencies, refining charges and the net smelter return base by property, which the royalty and mining tax calculations use.

error.defect_description: Royalty-bearing ounces not split by property.

evidence.note: The Eagle River mine is subject to a 2% net smelter return royalty, so each sale feeds the royalty base (wdofs2021). Times: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Update cash forecast and send outturn to the mill
steps.description: The manager updates the cash forecast and treasury report with the proceeds and the metal still held, and forwards the final outturn to the mill metallurgist for the month-end true-up.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors from earlier steps pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Outturn variance queried with the mill
exceptions.description: The refinery's weights or assays differ from the shipment advice beyond tolerance and the manager asks the mill to check its figures before selling.

exceptions.name: Umpire assay
exceptions.description: The mill disputes the refinery assay and a split goes to an umpire laboratory, delaying the final figure by weeks.

exceptions.name: Sale held or resized by the CFO
exceptions.description: The CFO asks for part of the metal to be held for a better price or quarter-end cash, and the manager re-proposes.

exceptions.name: Settlement break
exceptions.description: Cash arrives short or late or the metal transfer is missed, and the accountant traces it with the bank and the refinery.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from refinery outturn to sale booked and cash forecast updated
benchmarks.population: Small listed Canadian gold producer selling at spot

evidence.note: One or two days to check the outturn and get approval, two business days to settlement (lbmaotc), and one to three days to match and book; author's estimate.
Gold revenue of 215,294 thousand in 2020 (wdofs2021) over 91,229 oz sold (wdomda2021) gives about 2,360 per oz.
No gold price hedge contracts in place as at or during 2021 and 2020; no forward exchange contracts.

pain_points.description: Outturn checks are done by hand against a spreadsheet of the mine's bar figures, and variances need emails to the mill and sometimes an umpire assay that holds the final figure for weeks.

evidence.note: Settlement waits for negotiation or umpire analysis when results differ (lbmavar2017).

pain_points.description: One treasury manager runs proposal, dealing and metal transfers, so sales wait when that person or the CFO is away.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Trades, metal transfers and cash are matched across separate bank and refinery portals and email, with re-keying into the ERP and the sales register.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common practice for small listed Canadian gold producers selling refined gold to bullion banks, 2019-2022.

assumptions: Simulated median cycle time is about 6.8 days against a tier C estimate of 5 days: queue waits at eight desk steps add up in series, while in practice the manager often checks, proposes and sells on the same day. The gap is within the range of the estimate's uncertainty and the waits were left as they are.

The organisation file says gold is sold 'on spot or against forward contracts'. The company's 2021 statements say it had no gold hedge or forward exchange contracts in 2020 or 2021 (wdofs2021), so this workflow models spot sales only.

The 2022 technical report says gold is sold to 'various banks and refineries'; the statements say financial institutions only. Banks are modelled; a refinery purchase would follow the same steps with the refinery as buyer.
One case is the ounces from one refinery outturn, sold in one decision; where an outturn is split into several trades the trade steps repeat but are not modelled separately.

The corporate accountant, corporate controller and mill superintendent take part although the organisation file lists only the treasury and tax manager and the CFO for this process; segregation of duties needs someone other than the trader to match confirmations and cash.
Staffing check: hands-on time times five sales a month implies about 0.2 FTE, and the roles state about 0.19 FTE, mostly the treasury and tax manager and the corporate accountant.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.30 for staff; executive rates are cash compensation only).
